chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Fats Waller's radio show and the Ink Spots in Cincinnati
summary: Fats Waller had the Rhythm Club show on WLW, replaced by the Ink Spots, whose member Hoppy got his name there.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Was Fats staying in that part of the country?
Yeah, he was staying in Cincinnati at the time. He had a show at WOLW called the Rhythm Club.
Which was taken from the Rhythm Club up here in Harlem. And I mean it was named after that you know. And he had a kind of act on there. That's when the first time the INK Spots got to be known.

Fats had a little disagreement I think with the management of WOLW, so they hired the Ink Spots to take that place. And they had a guy in there called Hoppy (PHONETIC) [inserted: John] in that show. And Hoppy (PHONETIC) -- and that was Hoppy (PHONETIC) -- that was the guy's name that was with the INK Spots. That's how he got the name Hoppy (PHONETIC).
It was because -- you know -- had that character and kept calling him Hoppy (PHONETIC) when they got to be the Ink Spots. Do you understand?
